gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the adapter you need for 25W depends on which charger you use. Apple's MagSafe Charger needs an adapter offering 15V/2.0A (a 30W or larger USB-C adapter is the example). Third-party Qi2.2 pads ask for more: ESR Cyclone ≥35W input, and UGREEN MagFlow Pro pages say '45W Adapter Required' or '45W+ Input for 25W'. So a 30W adapter that works for Apple's charger may not give a third-party pad its full 25W. None of the results say whether one of those pads drops to 15W or 20W on a 30W adapter. Also missing: an older MagSafe Charger marked A2580 or A3250 already gives an iPhone 17 the 25W tier, while A2140 is capped at 15W, and the iPhone 17e is a 15W phone.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Apple iPhone 17 specs page, which says 'MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W' and 'Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W', with footnote 6 saying '…up to 25W with 30W power adapter or higher'. Also compared against the cited MagSafe Charger (1 m) product page, whose only footnote describes testing with a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter. Neither page gives the 15V/2.0A requirement. Neither lists which older MagSafe Charger part numbers (A2580, A3250 vs A2140) reach 25W. Neither says the iPhone 17e is limited to 15W. And neither covers the higher adapter wattage that third-party Qi2.2 pads need. ChatGPT's answer copied the generic 'a 30W or higher USB-C power adapter for Apple's MagSafe Charger' line and stopped there.
decides: This changes how the page should frame the adapter column and the cost. With a 30W adapter the shopper already owns, Apple's MagSafe Charger ($39/$49), including an A2580 or A3250 unit they may already have, reaches the 25W tier. The ESR Cyclone needs a 35W or larger adapter for 25W, and the UGREEN MagFlow Pro pad needs 45W. So the cost of each pad should include the adapter it needs. The kits that ship with a 45–50W adapter (Belkin WIZ040, Anker Prime 3-in-1, ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1) skip the problem. The iPhone 17e should be flagged as 15W on any charger. The ESR listing also asks for a magnetic case no thicker than 2 mm, which belongs in the fit notes.
